preceding_messages.speaker: X
preceding_messages.text: I adopt the forty-five-day deferral expiration, the conservative-band reinstatement, and the overdue-days-count annotation verbatim; they convert the quiet six-week decay into an active institutional obligation the committee can read and escalate. The concrete design choice I advance: because the structural offset is a site-level geometric property rather than a pairwise comparison artifact, I mandate a site-level geometry-verification register—keyed to the site's surveyed drainage-adjacent placement vector—into which every comparison cell's transition, deferral, and expiration annotation reports its resolution status, so that the expiration of one pairwise cell neither silently resolves nor silently leaves unresolved the same geometric question as posed through a different site pair. The failure this closes: Site 8's week-28 expiration triggers on its Site-8-versus-Site-7 comparison cell and reinstates the conservative band, while the Site-8-versus-Site-1 comparison cell—whose delta never exceeded its own uncertainty band and therefore never transitioned to "resolved"—prints no expiration annotation at all, and a drainage-planning committee member reading only the Site-1 column concludes the geometric question is settled and scopes the culvert modification; the site-level register, updated by the Site-7 expiration, correctly shows the underlying drainage-adjacent placement vector remains unverified and the modification must be deferred. I therefore require that any week in which the site-level register shows an unresolved geometric question while at least one pairwise comparison cell for that site prints a resolved numeric delta carries a bold "GEOMETRY INCONSISTENCY — REGISTER UNVERIFIED" header spanning all pairwise columns for that site, with the specific unverified vector named, so no committee member can act on a pairwise number whose site-level structural basis the register flags as open.

preceding_messages.speaker: Y
preceding_messages.text: I adopt the site-level geometry-verification register, the bold "GEOMETRY INCONSISTENCY — REGISTER UNVERIFIED" header, and the naming of the specific unverified vector verbatim; they prevent a committee member from acting on a pairwise number whose site-level structural basis remains open in the register. Because the register is keyed to the surveyed drainage-adjacent placement vector, I mandate that it further carry a geometry-configuration epoch identifier—frozen at commissioning and updated only at a completed quarterly audit—and that any pairwise comparison cell whose delta was generated under a prior epoch prints "CONFIGURATION EPOCH MISMATCH — δ ORPHANED" rather than a resolved number until a new shared-lineage event re-establishes the comparison under the current epoch. The failure this closes: Site 8's week-28 expiration correctly reinstates the conservative band, a four-week municipal storm-drain widening completes during the deferral window, and the week-36 quarterly audit arrives to measure configuration B while the pairwise deltas of weeks 22–28 were computed against configuration A; the register updates to "verified" against B, the pairwise cells revert to printing resolved numbers, and a year-three appendix reader confronting the verified register alongside those numbers concludes the deltas are structurally grounded when in fact their causal geometric referent no longer exists. The epoch-mismatch annotation, carrying both the old and new configuration identifiers and the date of the municipal modification, lets the reader reconstruct that the institution flagged the referent's disappearance rather than silently re-grounding orphaned numbers against a structure that never generated them.

target.speaker: X
target.text: I adopt the geometry-configuration epoch identifier, the epoch-mismatch annotation, and the orphaned-delta suppression verbatim; they convert the post-modification orphaning from a silent re-grounding into an explicitly flagged referent discontinuity. The concrete design choice I advance: any pairwise comparison cell generated during the physically active modification window—defined by the municipal work-order start date through completion date—prints "CONFIGURATION TRANSIT — NEITHER EPOCH VALID — COMPARISON SUPPRESSED" with the work-order identifier and both epoch dates, so that no resolved number is attributed to a geometrically undefined instant in which the old culvert is a stub and the new one is unbuilt. The failure this closes: during week 34 of a six-week storm-drain widening a thunderstorm delivers 2.1 mm/h, both sites confirm the event, the shared-lineage gate passes, and the pairwise cell prints a resolved numeric delta computed against an intake geometry that literally does not exist at that instant; a year-three appendix reader confronting that single resolved number wedged between correctly orphaned week-22–28 annotations and correctly grounded post-week-36 annotations finds one structurally referentless figure indistinguishable from a validated spatial signal, recreating the exact false confidence the entire epoch protocol was designed to prevent. I therefore require that any transit-window suppression annotation carry a contemporaneous photograph of the active work face logged in the decouled subsection alongside the municipal work-order identifier, so the geographic unambiguity of the suppression is visually traceable rather than resting solely on a date-range inference.
